stops.name: Marib, the Sabaean capital and the Great Dam
stops.campa: In the red land between the deserts stands Marib, seat of Saba, where the wadi Dhana is bridled by a wall of earth and stone longer than a marching army: the Great Dam that turns flood into orchard. Two sluices breathe water into a green oasis; palm and vine and grain rise where sand should be. The queen's storehouses hold gold from the south and the pale tears of the incense trees. Almaqah the god is worshipped; the sun is honored in the high places. From here the caravan roads run north to the sea of nations.
stops.quote: Indeed, I found [there] a woman ruling them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne.

stops.name: The Temple of Awwam (Mahram Bilqis), Marib
stops.campa: South of the city, ringed by a great oval wall, stands the sanctuary the later ages will call Mahram Bilqis: the Sanctuary of the Queen. Here Almaqah, the moon-bull of Saba, receives frankincense on his altars; pilgrims process between eight tall pillars into the sacred oval. The queen makes offering as her fathers did, mistress of a people who worship the host of heaven. Yet a rumor travels the incense roads with the caravans: that in the north a king named Solomon knows the speech of birds and the names of God.
stops.quote: I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds pleasing to them.

stops.name: The Frankincense Groves of Dhofar
stops.campa: Eastward along the incense coast the Boswellia trees grow from bare rock, wounded by the harvesters' blades so that the wound weeps a milky resin that hardens into pearls of frankincense. This is the treasure the whole known world burns before its gods: Egypt, Babylon, Israel. The queen's wealth is smoke: the roads that carry it, the wells that water it, the wall of Marib that feeds the men who walk it. She resolves to bring this treasure herself to the throne of the king who has heard of her god.

stops.name: Aksum, the Ethiopian Throne of Makeda
stops.campa: Across the strait, in the highlands of Ethiopia, the same queen sits, for the Kebra Nagast keeps her here, Makeda, ruler of a realm that reaches from Aksum to the incense sea. Her merchant Tamrin returns from the north drunk with wonder at Solomon's wisdom and justice, at the palace he builds for the God of Israel. Makeda listens, and a fire kindles in her: she will not send tribute, she will go herself. She commands the caravan made ready: camels beyond counting, gold, gems, and the frankincense of the south.
stops.quote: I am smitten with the love of wisdom... for wisdom is far better than treasure of gold and silver, and wisdom is the best of everything that hath been created on the earth.
stops.quote_source: Kebra Nagast, ch. 24 (Budge), Makeda resolves to journey

stops.name: Solomon's Court, the Muster of the Birds
stops.campa: In Jerusalem, Solomon, to whom God has taught the speech of birds and given command over wind and jinn, reviews his winged host. He finds one place empty. 'Why do I not see the hoopoe? Or is he among the absent? I will surely punish him or slaughter him, unless he brings me clear authority.' The ranks of the birds stand silent under the king's anger; the small brown crested bird is nowhere in the sky. Then, from the south, a shape comes beating over the desert with news.
stops.quote: And he inspected the birds and said, 'Why do I not see the hoopoe — or is he among the absent? I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or slaughter him unless he brings me clear authorization.'

stops.name: The Hoopoe's Report of Saba
stops.campa: The hoopoe alights and speaks without fear: 'I have encompassed that which you have not, and I have come to you from Saba with certain news.' He tells of a woman who rules there, given every good thing, with a mighty throne, but he found her and her people bowing to the sun, turned by Satan from the way of God. Solomon does not strike the bird. 'We will see,' he says, 'whether you were truthful or were of the liars.' He writes a letter and seals it, and gives it into the beak of the bird.
stops.quote: I have encompassed [in knowledge] that which you have not encompassed, and I have come to you from Saba with certain news.

stops.name: The Letter in the Bird's Beak, delivered to the Queen
stops.campa: The hoopoe flies south and drops the sealed letter into the queen's own court. She takes it up and reads it aloud to her chiefs: 'A noble letter has been delivered to me. It is from Solomon, and it is: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Be not haughty with me, but come to me in submission.' The words are few and the summons is total: not to tribute but to God. The queen, wise, will not answer alone.
stops.quote: Indeed, it is from Solomon, and indeed, it reads: 'In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Be not haughty with me but come to me in submission [as Muslims].'

stops.name: The Council of the Chiefs, Saba
stops.campa: The queen sets the matter before her lords: 'O eminent ones, advise me in my affair. I would not decide a matter until you witness for me.' They answer that they are strong and fierce in war, yet the command is hers. She is wiser than her warriors. 'Indeed kings, when they enter a city, ruin it and render the honored of its people humbled. And thus do they do.' She will not meet strength with strength. First she will test him: send a gift, and watch what the messengers bring back.
stops.quote: Indeed kings — when they enter a city, they ruin it and render the honored of its people humbled. And thus do they do.

stops.name: The Testing Gift Sent to Solomon
stops.campa: She sends a rich present ahead by envoys. But when it reaches Solomon he is unmoved and stern: 'Do you provide me with wealth? What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you. Rather, it is you who rejoice in your gift.' He bids the envoy return, with a threat of hosts the queen cannot withstand, and expulsion in disgrace. The message is unmistakable: this king wants no gold. He wants the queen herself, and her surrender to God. Now she knows she must go north in person.
stops.quote: Do you provide me with wealth? But what Allah has given me is better than what He has given you. Rather, it is you who rejoice in your gift.

stops.name: Najran, the Parting of the Roads
stops.campa: The caravan sets out along the incense road, and the first great oasis is Najran, where the north and south routes divide among the palms. Camels beyond number bear the queen's treasure: gold, gems, and above all the spices, so much frankincense that no such quantity of it will ever come again. Wells are drawn, beasts are watered, guides are hired for the long dry stages ahead. The queen rides toward a king she has never seen, carrying with her the hard questions she has prepared to prove him.
stops.quote: She came to Jerusalem with a very great train, with camels that bare spices, and very much gold, and precious stones.

stops.name: Dedan (Al-'Ula), the Oasis Waystation
stops.campa: Weeks into the wilderness the road threads the sandstone canyons of Dedan, green with date-gardens fed by hidden springs. Here the caravans of all the incense lands rest and trade under the cliffs. The queen's train, with its dark tents, kneeling camels, and smoke of cook-fires, draws the desert's eyes. She hears again, at every well, the fame of Solomon joined to the name of the LORD his God, and the reports only sharpen her resolve to see with her own eyes whether the half of it is true.
stops.quote: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to prove him with hard questions.

stops.name: Tayma, the Great Desert Well
stops.campa: At Tayma, oldest of the northern oases, the famed well and its ringed wall sustain the caravan across the edge of the Nafud sands. The queen rehearses her riddles in the cool of the tents: the questions she will lay before the king to catch his wisdom, of which the whole road speaks. Ahead lie Petra's ravines and the highlands of Judah. The frankincense goes on ahead of her like a promise of smoke; she comes behind it, a queen bearing the wealth of the south to the city of the God of Israel.
